title: "Shake 'n' Bake" Method: A Closed-System Reaction Simulation
description: An academic simulation providing a theoretical overview of the 'one-pot' or 'shake 'n' bake' method for chemical synthesis. This process is known for its use of a single, sealed reaction vessel. This is for educational purposes only, to study reaction kinetics and gas pressure in a closed system.
objective: To theoretically model a one-pot reduction reaction and manage the resulting gas pressure to prevent a simulated vessel rupture.
principles: This simulation models a reaction where an alkali metal (lithium) and an oxidizing agent (ammonium nitrate) react in the presence of water to create ammonia gas and a strong reducing environment. The primary challenge is not the chemistry itself, but managing the extreme pressure buildup of ammonia gas in a sealed container, making it a powerful lesson in the dangers of closed-system reactions.

steps.title: Reagent Preparation
steps.action: In this theoretical model, the process begins by crushing pseudoephedrine tablets and adding them to the reaction vessel.
steps.detail: This increases the surface area for the reaction, a fundamental concept for increasing reaction rates.

steps.title: Addition of Oxidizer
steps.action: Ammonium nitrate, theoretically sourced from cold packs, is added to the vessel.
steps.detail: This component will react with the lithium to generate the ammonia gas that drives the pressure system in this simulation.

steps.title: Introduction of a Reducing Agent
steps.action: Lithium metal, theoretically sourced from batteries, is added.
steps.detail: Lithium is a powerful reducing agent that drives the chemical transformation of the starting material.

steps.title: Reaction Initiation
steps.action: A small amount of water and a non-polar solvent are added to the mixture.
steps.detail: The water initiates the highly exothermic reaction between the ammonium nitrate and lithium, which begins to produce ammonia gas almost immediately.

steps.title: Pressure Management
steps.action: The vessel is sealed and shaken to mix the reagents. The reaction produces ammonia gas, which must be periodically vented.
steps.detail: This is the most dangerous and critical step in the theoretical process. The simulation requires the user to monitor a pressure gauge and vent the gas to prevent a simulated vessel rupture.

steps.title: Theoretical Product Extraction
steps.action: After the reaction is complete, the liquid is separated, and the final product is extracted from the non-polar solvent.
steps.detail: This simulation concludes when the theoretical product is isolated after successfully managing the pressure cycle.

tips: The primary learning objective of this simulation is understanding the immense danger of gas-producing reactions in sealed containers.
In this model, the rate of shaking directly impacts the reaction rate and thus the speed of pressure buildup.
